title: 1Password account security changes
volume: None on a normal day. Each rule takes one audit event for one admin action, so an account sees a few a month, most of them admins changing settings on purpose.
mdr_note: These detections are yours to work. Sophos MDR doesn't work custom detections, and a case your own case rule opens from them is Managed By Self.
author: Aaronjacobs000
summary: Four custom detection rules for 1Password Business, on the CloudAudit records the library's 1Password parsers write from the Events API. They make a detection when someone exports a vault, turns off multi-factor authentication or Unlock with SSO, changes the firewall rules or starts an account recovery. Each rule matches sensor type 1Password only.
notes:
Setup:
- Add the library's 1Password Business parsers and the example bridge in bridges/1password-events first, then run the check-your-data search to see audit events arrive.
- These rules read audit events, so keep auditevents in the bridge's ONEPASSWORD_FEATURES and in the token's Events to Report.

How it works:
- 1Password names each audit event by its object and action, such as vault.export or account.disblmfa, and the parser writes that as the event name.
- The sign-in protection rule takes multi-factor authentication turned off for the whole account (account.disblmfa) or for one person (user.disblmfa), and Unlock with SSO turned off (sso.disblsso).
- The export rule reads the audit event for a vault export, not item usage. Item usage logs an export for every item exported and every file downloaded, so it would make one detection per item.

Tuning:
- If one admin changes firewall rules as part of their job, leave them out in the query itself, such as and user_name != 'netadmin@example.com'. A suppression rule would hide Sophos's detections for that user as well.

Testing:
- In a lab tenant on 2026-11-22, each query returned exactly the sample lines tests.json lists in Data Lake Search, and the rules run offline on the same 10 records agreed. Data Lake Search didn't find the records while they kept their October dates, so the samples went in with their dates moved to the test day.
- As live rules there, each one fired on exactly its sample lines within about two minutes. Copies sent in the first minutes after the parsers were turned on made only some of these detections or none; the same lines sent 20 minutes later made every one.
- No Sophos detector made a detection on the lines these rules take. Sophos's sign-in analytics flagged only the sample sign-ins on Auth, as an unseen user, address or application.

Known gaps:
- Sign-in attempts, item reveals and shares, and group changes have no rule. Search them when you need them.
- An audit event names a group by its UUID only, so a rule can't tell that someone joined the Administrators or Owners group.
